system_note: Full-claim DRG audit MR_25 - determination: Finding. Summary of what was billed vs. what the record supports, with citations. 1) Principal diagnosis / sepsis grouping - Billed principal: A40.3 (Sepsis due to Streptococcus pneumoniae) in position 1 with R65.21 (severe sepsis with septic shock) as additional MCC. Provider documentation and microbiology support organism-specific sepsis. Evidence: admitting H&P documents septic shock with lactate 5.1 mmol/L and intubation for respiratory failure (History & Physical, p.57 [NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_25.pdf-n9]); Infectious Diseases documents admission blood cultures that grew Streptococcus pneumoniae (Infectious Diseases Consultation, p.43 [NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_25.pdf-n50]). The sepsis policy requires provider documentation of sepsis and (for R65.21) septic shock / vasopressor/lactate evidence; the chart documents vasopressors (Discharge/Transfer Summary, p.837 [NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_25.pdf-n1125]) and high lactate on presentation, satisfying the policy criteria for R65.21 alongside an organism-specific A40.- code (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Sepsis-and-Septic-Shock.docx-b8). Conclusion: A40.3 (principal) and R65.21 (additional, MCC) are supported by documentation (evidence: ev_0001, ev_0004, pol_001). 2) Pneumonia and organism coding - Billed: J13 (pneumonia due to Streptococcus pneumoniae) and B96.5 (Pseudomonas as cause elsewhere). Admission and course support community-acquired Streptococcus pneumoniae pneumonia on presentation (H&P/problem list and ID consult - ev_0001) and a later hospital-acquired Pseudomonas ventilator-associated infection (ICU progress notes, radiology, and discharge summary documenting resolved VAP due to Pseudomonas - ev_0002, ev_0003, ev_0006). Conclusion: J13 and B96.5 are supported when coded to reflect admission organism (Strep pneumo) and subsequent VAP organism (Pseudomonas) as documented. 3) Respiratory failure and ARDS - Billed: J96.01 (acute respiratory failure with hypoxia, MCC) and J80 (ARDS, MCC). The chart documents hypoxemic respiratory failure requiring emergent intubation and mechanical ventilation (H&P: PaO2 58 on HFNC, intubation for hypoxemia; ev_0001) and later ABG/P/F ratios and imaging consistent with ARDS (Nephrology and ICU notes showing P/F 71, chest films with bilateral opacities; inpatient problem list and discharge summary list ARDS and ARDS management with proning;, ev_0007). Conclusion: J96.01 and J80 are supported and appropriately carry MCC weight (policy: J96.01 and J80 validation criteria satisfied - evidence: ev_0001, ev_0007; policy excerpts: RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Acute-Respiratory-Failure-with-Hypoxia.docx-b8 and RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Acute-Respiratory-Distress-Syndrome-ARDS-.docx-b8 were reviewed). 4) Acute kidney injury / dialysis dependence - Billed: N17.9 (AKI, CC) and Z99.2 (dependence on renal dialysis, POA=N). Nephrology documents oliguric AKI meeting criteria for renal replacement therapy and initiation of CRRT (Nephrology Consultation, p.677 - ). Discharge documents renal recovery and dialysis discontinued (Discharge Summary, p.837 - ev_0004). Conclusion: N17.9 is supported (CC); Z99.2 POA=N also supported for dialysis dependence during the stay. 5) Ventilator-associated pneumonia (J95.851): POA and severity - Billed: J95.851 with POA=N and flagged CC on claim. The medical record documents onset of pneumonia while mechanically ventilated (ICU progress note: 'day-6 VAP' / new right basilar consolidation and broadening to cefepime per ID; Radiology: 'New right basilar consolidation - suspected ventilator-associated pneumonia'; Infectious Diseases: 'day-6 VAP') (ev_0002, ev_0003, /ev_0006). Policy: J95.851 is an MCC-level code and must carry POA = N for hospital-acquired VAP (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Ventilator-Associated-Pneumonia.docx-b8). Conclusion: J95.851 is supported by documentation, but its CC flag on the claim is incorrect - it should be MCC and POA=N. Evidence supporting VAP onset >48 hours post-intubation and organism-directed therapy is cited (ev_0002, ev_0003, ev_0006, pol_002). 6) Pulmonary embolism (I26.99) - unsupported - Billed: I26.99 (other pulmonary embolism without cor pulmonale) POA=Y, MCC. Review of imaging and consults does not support a diagnosis of PE. Cardiology's CT Chest with IV contrast specifically documents 'no pulmonary embolism' (Cardiology Consultation, p.122 - ev_0005). Discharge/transfer documentation and procedure/medication lists document catheter-associated right IJ DVT and anticoagulation but do NOT document an in-hospital pulmonary embolism in the imaging/consultation or discharge summary (ev_0004, ev_0005). Conclusion: I26.99 is not supported by the retrieved chart and should be removed from the coded diagnosis set (evidence: ev_0005, ev_0004). 7) Other billed comorbidities / status codes - New-onset atrial fibrillation (I48.91), delirium (F05), ICU-acquired weakness / critical illness myopathy (G72.81), catheter-associated right IJ DVT (I82.C11) and chronic comorbidities (E11.65, J44.9, I10, E78.5) are documented in consults, problem lists, and discharge summary (ev_0007, ev_0004). POA flags (Y vs N) are consistent with the clinical timeline (e.g., AF and DVT developed during stay => POA=N). Conclusion: keep these codes as billed (no sequencing change needed). Corrective actions taken (claim-level): - Remove unsupported diagnosis I26.99 (no imaging/consult support) (evidence: Cardiology CT 'no pulmonary embolism' and lack of PE mention on discharge - ev_0005, ev_0004). - Remove spurious/invalid claim line '7204' (no corresponding documentation in the medical record / not a valid ICD-10 diagnosis) - no supporting documentation found in chart sections that list principal problems (INPATIENT MEDICAL RECORD, p.1 shows principal diagnoses and no 7204) (ev_0007). - Update J95.851 (Ventilator-associated pneumonia) severity from CC to MCC and retain POA = N (evidence: ICU progress note, radiology, ID consult, discharge summary; policy says J95.851 is MCC and requires POA = N) (ev_0002, ev_0003, ev_0006, pol_002). Revised diagnosis & procedure lists (complete corrected lists appear in the code_decisions and revised_* fields). Key policy citations used: R65.21 / organism-specific sepsis guidance (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Sepsis-and-Septic-Shock.docx-b8) and VAP POA/severity rules (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Ventilator-Associated-Pneumonia.docx-b8). Reviewer conclusion: Finding due to an unsupported pulmonary embolism diagnosis (I26.99) and an incorrect CC severity flag on J95.851 (should be MCC). All other billed diagnoses and procedures are supported by provider documentation and meet the governing policy criteria cited above (evidence list: ev_0001-pol_002).
rationale_letter: Re: DRG audit MR_25 - Determination letter Dear Provider, We performed a clinical coding review of the above-referenced inpatient encounter (admit 2026-09-27 to transfer 2027-02-06). Our audit compared the billed diagnosis and procedure codes to the treating medical record and the applicable DRG coding policies. This letter summarizes our findings, the clinical basis for the determination, and the corrections we are making to the claim. Finding After review, we have determined that one billed diagnosis lacks clinical support and one diagnosis's severity flag is miscoded. Specifically: 1) I26.99 (Other pulmonary embolism without acute cor pulmonale) - REMOVED. Rationale: contemporaneous diagnostic imaging (CT chest with IV contrast) and cardiology consultation document no pulmonary embolism; the record documents catheter-associated right internal jugular DVT but no imaging or provider statement confirming pulmonary embolism (Cardiology Consultation, CT Chest: '...no pulmonary embolism.' - ev_0005). Because the clinical record does not support a diagnosis of PE, this code is not valid for this encounter and will be removed. 2) J95.851 (Ventilator-associated pneumonia) - SEVERITY FLAG ADJUSTED. Rationale: the treating clinicians document a ventilator-associated pneumonia developing on day 6 of mechanical ventilation (ICU progress note and ID consult show 'day-6 VAP' with new right basilar consolidation on chest radiograph; radiology impression: 'New right basilar consolidation - suspected ventilator-associated pneumonia.' - ev_0002, ev_0003). Per the VAP policy guidance, J95.851 is an MCC-level code and must carry POA = N when onset is >48 hours after intubation (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Ventilator-Associated-Pneumonia.docx-b8 - pol_002). The chart supports hospital-acquired VAP due to Pseudomonas treated with cefepime (Discharge/Transfer Summary: 'resolved ventilator-associated pneumonia (Pseudomonas)'; ICU/ID notes confirm the timing and treatment - ev_0006, ev_0002, ev_0003), therefore J95.851 should be classified as MCC. The claim currently lists this line as CC; we are correcting the severity to MCC and retaining POA = N. Supporting documentation relied upon - Admission H&P and ED documentation showing septic shock on presentation with lactate 5.1 mmol/L and intubation for hypoxemic respiratory failure (History & Physical, 2026-09-27 - ev_0001). - Infectious Diseases consultation documenting admission blood cultures positive for Streptococcus pneumoniae (Infectious Diseases Consultation, 2026-10-02 - ). - ICU progress notes documenting new purulent secretions, rising WBC, new right-sided consolidation and a day-6 VAP assessment with broadened antimicrobials per ID (Critical Care Progress Note, 2026-10-02 - ev_0002). - Chest radiograph interpretation documenting new right basilar consolidation suspicious for VAP (Diagnostic Imaging Report, 2026-10-02 - ev_0003). - Discharge/Transfer Summary documenting hospital course including vasopressor use (norepinephrine/vasopressin), CRRT/HD for AKI with subsequent recovery, tracheostomy and resolved Pseudomonas VAP (Discharge / Transfer Summary, 2027-02-06 - ev_0004, ev_0006). - Cardiology consult documentation including CT chest finding of no pulmonary embolism (Cardiology Consultation, 2026-09-30 - ev_0005). - Nephrology consult documenting oliguric AKI needing renal replacement therapy (Nephrology Consultation, 2026-09-29 - ). Corrections to the claim - Removed diagnosis: I26.99 (Other pulmonary embolism without acute cor pulmonale). - Removed spurious code/line: '7204' (no supporting documentation / not a valid coded diagnosis in the record). - Updated diagnosis severity: J95.851 (Ventilator-associated pneumonia) - change from CC to MCC; POA remains N. - All other billed diagnoses and procedures retained as billed (A40.3, R65.21, J13, J96.01, J80, N17.9, B96.5, I48.91, F05, G72.81, I82.C11, E11.65, J44.9, I10, E78.5, Z99.11, Z99.2, and the billed procedures). If you disagree with this determination, please supply any additional contemporaneous provider documentation (progress notes, imaging reports, consultant notes, microbiology) that specifically confirm a pulmonary embolism during this admission or that would change the VAP severity assignment. Provide such documentation within the appeals period described in your contract/policy. Sincerely, Clinical Audit Team Cascadia Regional Medical Center Audit Review (References to the specific supporting record passages are available in the enclosed audit evidence list: ev_0001-pol_002.)
